headline: Scientists Grow Fabric From Living Fungus That Cleans Itself
meta_description: Researchers at a Chinese institute have created biodegradable fabric from Cordyceps militaris fungus that self-cleans and repairs itself when damaged.
summary_short: A research team grew wearable fabric from living fungus that can clean itself, repair tears, and fully biodegrade in 41 days—opening new possibilities for sustainable fa…
body:
Scientists at the Shenzredan Institutes of Advanced Technology have created a fabric entirely from a living organism: Cordyceps militaris, a fungus traditionally used in Chinese medicine. The material grows from fine threadlike filaments called hyphae that naturally weave into dense networks. Researchers cultivated the fungus into small pellets, pressed them into flexible sheets, and added glycerol to make them pliable—producing a fabric that can clean itself and repair its own tears when fresh fungal pellets are placed on damaged spots.

What makes this approach genuinely novel is its flexibility as a platform. The fungal matrix can host other microorganisms to gain new properties: the team added engineered yeast for color and melanin-rich fungus for UV protection, demonstrating what they call a "plug-and-play" system where different organisms can be layered in without changing the base material. Environmental testing showed the fabric fully degraded within 41 days—a stark contrast to synthetic textiles that persist for decades.

Yet the path to mainstream clothing remains distant. The cost structure presents a significant barrier: the culture medium accounts for more than 95 percent of production expenses. Near-term applications lie instead in temporary uses—short-run fashion, exhibition pieces, art installations, and biodegradable packaging. The research team is working to reduce outside inputs by having the fungus produce its own pigments and functional molecules, with longer-term goals involving synthetic gene circuits that could activate biological functions only at specific times or locations. The technology reveals how innovation in sustainable fashion may come not from refining old materials, but from growing entirely new ones.
quick_facts: Cordyceps militaris fungus grown into self-cleaning, self-repairing fabric
Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, China
